decisions.reason: As a flagship digital patient and consent app, it builds directly on existing clinical and compliance software knowledge, giving the firm strong absorptive capacity to interpret feedback and improve it.
The continuing education institute leverages the firm's existing training content and support capabilities, so the firm can assimilate and enhance this offering with related knowledge.

A remote screen-sharing tool is a generic support utility that does not build on domain-specific dental software knowledge, limiting the firm's ability to improve it and making it a likely candidate for removal.
The performance analytics dashboard draws on practice management data and the firm's software engineering expertise, enabling the firm to interpret early usage data and refine the product.
The complete dental practice bundle consists of the firm's existing software modules and therefore is closest to its established knowledge and should be retained.

A job and practice listing portal requires marketplace and community-management capabilities unrelated to the firm's software and training knowledge, so its limited absorptive capacity makes dropping it likely.
